 IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/CIVIL APPLICATION (FOR CONDONATION OF DELAY) NO. 235 of  2026  In R/CROSS OBJECTION/42/2026  In R/FIRST APPEAL/4200/2022  With  R/CROSS OBJECTION NO. 42 of 2026  In  R/FIRST APPEAL NO. 4200 of 2022  ==========================================================
 LH OF PATEL SHANTILAL BABALDAS & ANR.
 Versus  GENERAL MANAGER,ONGC & ANR.
 ==========================================================
 Appearance:
 MR AV PRAJAPATI(672) for the Applicant(s) No. 1,1.1  MS.HIMANI SHAH, AGP for the Respondent(s) No. 2  GUPTA LAW ASSOCIATES(9818) for the Respondent(s) No. 1  ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MRS. JUSTICE M. K. THAKKER  Date : 03/02/2026  ORAL ORDER 1. Rule returnable forthwith.

Learned AGP Ms.Himani Shah waives service of notice of Rule on behalf of respondent No.2.
2.
This application is filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act for condonation of delay of 1118 days occurred in filing the Cross Objection No.38010 of 2025.

sentences.text: Learned advocate Mr. A. V. Prajapati for the applicants submits that the present cross-objections are filed in First Appeal No.4332 of 2022, which is admitted by this Court vide order dated 02.03.2023.

It is submitted by the NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/235/2026 ORDER DATED:
03/02/2026 undefined

learned advocate Mr.Prajapati that on 15.08.2025, the applicant came into the knowledge from one of the land- owners of adjacent village, Nugar, whose lands are also acquired that he had been granted enhanced compensation of Rs. 2,069.63/-.

Learned advocate Mr.
Prajapati further submits that the present applicant, being an agriculturist, would not have the knowledge of legal proceedings and he would waive the interest for the delayed period in the event of succeeding in the cross-objection.
4. Per contra, learned AGP Ms.Himani Shah has opposed the applications for condonation of delay.

5. This Court has referred to the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Suresh Kumar V/s. State of Haryana and Others reported in 2025 SCC Online SC 896, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that even though there was long delay in filing the appeals, it was a case of compulsory acquisition and there had been a difference in the amount of compensation granted to some land losers vis-a-vis others.

entities.text: Suresh Kumar V/s. State of Haryana and Others reported in 2025 SCC Online SC 896
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This Court has also referred to the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/235/2026 ORDER DATED:
03/02/2026 undefined

Market Committee Hodal V/s. Krishan Murari, reported in 1996 (1) SC 311,
wherein delay of 3240 daysarising from the same acquisition had been condoned.

entities.text: Market Committee Hodal V/s. Krishan Murari, reported in 1996 (1) SC 311
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This Court has also referred to the decision rendered by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Huchanagouda V/s.
Assistant Commissioner and Land Acquisition Officer, reported in 2020 (19) SCC 236, wherein the Court had taken into account the poverty and illiteracy of the land loser and condoned the delay of more than 2,000 days.

entities.text:
Huchanagouda V/s.
Assistant Commissioner and Land Acquisition Officer, reported in 2020 (19) SCC 236
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: While condoning the delay, the Hon'ble Apex Court had observed that equities had to be balanced by ensuring that the determination of market value relates back to the preliminary notification - making sure that there is no prejudice to the acquiring authorities, as also no undue advantage to the land loser.
5.1. It is observed by the Hon'ble Apex Court that the appellants who approached the Court with delay, would not be granted interest for such period.

Having considered the explanation offered in the application and the submissions made in the above paragraph No.3, this Court is of the considered view that the application NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/235/2026 ORDER DATED:
03/02/2026 undefined requires to be allowed and the delay of 1118 days is required to be condoned.
In that background, the present application is allowed and delay of 1118 days in filing the cross-objection is condoned.

6. It is needless to clarify that the applicants-original claimants shall not be entitled to the interest in event of the enhancement amount of compensation, if any, for the interregnum period i.e. from the date of pronouncement of the impugned judgment and award till the date of filing of the present appeal.
7. Copy of this order shall be placed in the docket of the first appeal.
Rule is made absolute.
ORDER IN R/CROSS OBJECTION NO. 42 of 2026
Cross-objection is admitted.
